text:
maria_cust: Hey @alex_support — we're seeing intermittent SSE disconnects and lots of partial/garbled JSON in the client. Happens when requests traverse our gRPC->HTTP1 gateway (Envoy) to Redwood's streaming endpoint. Billing also spiked because the client reconnects twice for the same user session. Repro attached below.

alex_support: Sorry to hear that, can you paste a minimal repro (curl or node) and a small snippet of the partial output? Also confirm whether tokens rotate mid-stream, and whether your gateway does any response buffering/flush batching.

maria_cust: Repro steps: client behind gRPC-Web gateway (Envoy) -> internal nginx -> redwood hosted endpoint. Node fetch normally but I can repro with curl. Example curl that reproduces partial chunking:

```
# HTTP/2 (direct works sometimes)
curl -v --http2 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?prompt=hello" > out-h2.txt

# HTTP/1.1 (via our gateway)
curl -v --http1.1 -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://gw.example/translate/stream?prompt=hello" > out-h1.txt
```

Partial output we see (client-side):
```
data: {"id":"msg-1","choices":[{"text":"Hel"}
# connection drops...
```
So chunks come back truncated ("Hel" instead of "Hello") and sometimes two small `data:` frames are merged into one token-less payload, which breaks our event parser.

alex_support: Thanks. A couple things to check: 1) do you see 401s or 403s mid-stream (token rotate)? 2) do your Envoy/nginx logs show `flush` calls or repeated small writes? 3) any intermediate HTTP/1.1 proxy versions that might coalesce chunks? Also give us a request_id from an affected request so we can correlate on our side.

maria_cust: We do see a 401 once in our logs when the client's short-lived token refresh happens. Log snippet on our side:

```
[2026-02-28T14:12:31Z] upstream_resp 200 request_id=abc123
[2026-02-28T14:12:33Z] upstream_resp 401 request_id=abc123 token=rotated
# client reconnects
[2026-02-28T14:12:34Z] upstream_resp 200 request_id=def456
```

Billing shows three units charged for what is logically one user session.

tyler_engruntime: Two separate but related issues likely: (A) HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation plus proxy buffering can coalesce or split SSE boundaries — small flushes get merged into one TCP packet or dropped until Nagle/coalescing happens on the gateway. (B) Mid-stream 401 + client reconnects result in multiple billed requests because each reconnect hits our usage meter.

Quick experiments to try:
- Compare direct HTTP/2 vs through gateway (`--http2` vs `--http1.1` curl) — you already did this which is helpful.
- Try forcing smaller write flushes on your gateway (disable response buffering), or enable `tcp_nodelay`/disable Nagle on the proxy side so chunks don't get merged.
- On our side we can add a `x-redwood-sse-force-flush: 1` response header to bias the proxy to flush immediately.

jasmin_prod: FYI we deployed a flush-batching optimization last week to reduce syscalls for high-cardinality streams; it batches tiny writes into a single flush every 20ms. That reduces overhead but can increase latency and can cause the “Hel” truncation symptom if a downstream proxy splits or reinterprets chunk boundaries. We should be able to toggle this per-customer while we investigate.

alex_support: Maria, can you share the exact request IDs of the billed sessions? We'll correlate with our logs and check if our meter counted each reconnect as a new billable request (likely) and whether we can provide a one-time credit while we patch.

maria_cust: Request IDs: abc123 (first), def456 (reconnect), ghi789 (second reconnect). Billing spike happened at 14:12:34-14:12:36. Also here's a node fetch snippet we used client-side:

```
const res = await fetch("https://gw.example/translate/stream?prompt=hi", {
  headers: { Accept: 'text/event-stream', Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
// read loop that parses `data: ` SSE framed chunks
```

When token refresh happens, we abort and re-open the stream — which triggers the duplicate billing.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-02-25T03:22:14Z - rolling update eng-runtime v1.14.2 applied to sse-flush-service

oncall_sre: Temporary mitigations for you to try:
1) Route traffic directly to our h2 ingress (bypass your gateway) to confirm it's gateway-related. `curl --http2` to our endpoint.
2) If bypass is not possible, set your Envoy config to disable response buffering and set `use_remote_address`/TCP_NODELAY for upstreams.
3) As a stopgap we can route your tenant to a compatibility path that disables flush-batching on our side (will increase CPU but reduces chunk coalescing).

tyler_engruntime: We'll open internal ticket RDW-9834 to add a per-tenant header `x-redwood-sse-force-flush: true` and an opt-out for the batching optimization. We'll also add an idempotency-hint header (e.g., `x-client-session-id`) we can use to dedupe billing events when a reconnect clearly belongs to an existing session. I'll also add telemetry to detect mid-stream 4xx/5xx followed by immediate reconnects and flag them.

alex_support: Maria, would you like us to temporarily move your org to the compatibility path (disable batching + enable force-flush) while engworks the permanent fix? That should stop the partial events and reduce duplicate billing.

maria_cust: Yes please — that would be ideal. Also can you advise on a short-term client change we can make? We can try pinning to h2 if we can reconfigure the gateway.

oncall_sre: Client-side short-term options:
- Prefer HTTP/2 end-to-end if possible. That avoids the h2->h1 translation problem. `curl --http2` is a good quick test.
- Add a jittered reconnect/backoff and include `x-client-session-id` on reconnects so we can correlate.
- Try to avoid aborting the connection mid-stream during token refresh; instead rotate tokens via an auth refresh endpoint and keep the stream alive if possible.

maria_cust: Ok we'll try direct h2 and ask our infra team about disabling response buffering in Envoy. Please go ahead and enable the compatibility path on your side. Thank you :pray:

alex_support: Done — I've requested RDW-SUPPORT-454 to move your tenant to the compatibility path. Tyler, assign RDW-9834 and cc billing for a one-time credit investigation.

tyler_engruntime: Assigned. I'll follow up here once we have a patch or telemetry. Thanks for the detailed repro — very helpful.

maria_cust: Great, much appreciated. Will report back after we try the bypass test.
